verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's first-party docs describe tenant tokens as short-lived, scoped credentials generated from an API key. They embed filters that automatically apply to every search request, so each user sees only their own data within a shared index, and the SaaS solution page states there is no need for separate indexes per customer. missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of tenant-token isolation in practice.

support.subject: As a developer, scoped or tenant tokens restrict each end user's searches to their own documents without separate indexes per user

citations.quote: Tenant tokens are short-lived, scoped credentials generated from an API key. They embed search rules (filters) that automatically apply to every search request, ensuring users only see their own data.
tenant tokens restrict what data each user can see within a shared index.
Each tenant gets isolated access through secure tokens. No need for separate indexes or infrastructure per customer.
Tenant tokens restrict search results to a specific tenant. Documents are filtered at query time.
